data.description:
# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

## Summary

Main Street side of the Steam follow-to-unlock feature (core CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC, F5). Adds a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action to the tutorial's final completion step (T26):

- `UnifiedTutorialStepDef.showSteamFollowCta` opt-in flag (T26 set).
- `MainStreetTutorialHints` renders the CTA in the completion tooltip: it opens the Steam store/community page through the launcher bridge (`window.tce.steamFollow`) when present, falls back to the web store page in a plain browser, and re-checks the follow (auto-detection, or the manual self-attest claim when the Steamworks binding has no `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`).
- The CTA is additive — the existing "Let's play!" button still finishes the tutorial; following is never required (graceful degradation).
- Copy added to `tutorial-en.csv` (`tutorial.steamFollow.*`), keeping the CSV integrity contract green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The tutorial's final step shows the Steam follow CTA (SLL-independent: it lives in the existing completion tooltip).
- [ ] Launcher mode opens the Steam page via the bridge; browser mode opens the web store page with copy explaining no reward is granted there.
- [ ] The follow is re-checked after the page opens; an unlock is surfaced as a status message.
- [ ] The CTA never blocks finishing the tutorial; a missing bridge or a rejected bridge call degrades to a status message.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the flag wiring, the CSV keys, and the bridge/browser branching.
- [ ] `npm test` (unit) and `npm run build` pass in this repo.

# Executive should grant an action point and a single hand slot

The Executive staff card (`staff-executive`) should be repurposed from a pure hand-capacity card into an action-economy card: while employed it grants **+1 action per week** and **+1 hand slot**. This extends the `actionsPerTurn` staff mechanic (introduced by MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0) to the tier-10 Executive and reduces its `handSlotsAdded` from `4` to `1`.

## Problem statement

The Executive is the tier-10 premium capacity card (`handSlotsAdded: 4`, cost 2000, ongoing 500) with no ability. Players who want a top-tier action-economy staff choice currently have only the tier-12 General Manager, so the Executive is a dead-end on the action-economy build axis. Granting the Executive `actionsPerTurn: 1` — traded against dropping its hand-slot bonus to a single slot — gives it a distinct, legible role.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a tier-10 action-economy staff option before the tier-12 General Manager is affordable.
- **Main Street player (mid/late game)** — wants the Executive's role to be clear: a tempo (extra action) card rather than a bulk hand-capacity card.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want to hire an Executive that grants +1 action per week and +1 hand slot so that I can take an extra action each week without waiting for the General Manager.
- As a Main Street player, I want the Executive's card art, tooltip and description to state the +1 action/week and the single hand slot so that I understand what I am buying.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `src/card-data.csv` `staff-executive` row sets `actionsPerTurn` to `1` and `handSlotsAdded` to `1` (down from `4`), keeping `cost: 2000`, `ongoingCost: 500`, tier `10`, and the generalist `allowedBusinessTypes` (`Food|Culture|Service|Commerce|Entertainment|Health`); the CSV `description` states the `+1` hand slot and the `+1` action/week (and no longer claims "major hand capacity" / `+4` slots). CSV column order is unchanged.
2. The parsed `StaffCard` template for `staff-executive` exposes `actionsPerTurn === 1` and `handSlotsAdded === 1`, and `executeWeekStart` composes the weekly budget as `1 base + sum(actionsPerTurn) + banked (capped at 2)` with the Executive included, preserving the existing invariants (staff actions consumed first, never banked; bank cap 2).
3. The staff card formatting and Actions HUD tooltip render the Executive's `Actions: +1/week` benefit and the in-game Help panel "Turn Flow" text lists the Executive among action-granting staff (Manager, Director, Executive, General Manager).
4. The committed card art `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/staff-executive.svg` is regenerated to show `+1 slots` (not `+4 slots`), and `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` matches the new `src/card-data.csv` content.
5. Tests assert the new Executive contract and no-regression for staff without the ability: `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` (Executive grants +1 action/turn and +1 slot; only Manager, Director, Executive and General Manager grant `actionsPerTurn`), `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (the Executive design-contract entry and the non-ability block are updated so the Executive is no longer listed as ability-free), and existing action-budget/tooltip tests remain green.
6. Documentation is updated to reflect the change: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ 6.0 action-economy staff list), `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (staff table), `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (staff catalogue row + rationale), and `docs/main-street/prd-multi-use-card-economy.md` (staff template table).
7. All related documentation and user-facing text (code comments/doc-strings, `README.md` where it references the affected card or the action list, in-game help panel) is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Mechanic already exists** — reuse `actionsPerTurn` (CSV column, `StaffCard.actionsPerTurn`, `executeWeekStart`, tooltip/formatting). No new engine mechanic, schema column, or save-format change is expected; the change is data + card art + docs + test coverage.
- Preserve the existing action-economy invariants: bank cap of 2, base-only banking, staff actions consumed first and never banked, and the defensive clamp in `executeWeekStart`.
- CSV column order must remain unchanged (edit in place); `actionsPerTurn` is already a known column.
- Do not alter the Manager, Director or General Manager as part of this item.
- Card SVG generation is driven by the CSV + `csv-checksum.json`; the committed SVG must be regenerated with the project generator (`node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) rather than hand-edited.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv`: `staff-executive` = `handSlotsAdded 4`, no `actionsPerTurn`, `cost 2000`, `ongoingCost 500`, tier 10, description "An experienced executive adds major hand capacity at a high ongoing cost."
- Action-granting staff today (MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0): Manager (tier 3, 700/250, +1 slot, +1 action), Director (tier 9, 1400/400, +3 slots, +1 action), General Manager (tier 12, 2000/500, +4 slots, +1 action). The Executive, Apprentice, Socialite, Accountant, Lookout, Investor and the specialization applicants do not grant actions.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` (`executeWeekStart`): budget = `1 + sum(staff.actionsPerTurn ?? 0) + min(2, bankedActions)` — logic is already generic.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` (staff case): renders `Actions: +N/week` when `actionsPerTurn > 0`; `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` (`buildActionTooltip`) appends the generic action-granting-staff note when any employed staff has `actionsPerTurn > 0`.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` "Turn Flow" body lists "(Manager, Director, General Manager)".
- Card art `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/staff-executive.svg` currently renders `+4 slots`; `csv-checksum.json` is committed alongside.
- Tests today: `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` (asserts the ladder and "only Manager, Director and General Manager grant `actionsPerTurn`"), `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (Executive contract `handSlotsAdded: 4`; Executive in the "staff without the ability" block), `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/staff-business-type-matching.test.ts` (Executive generalist — should remain unchanged).

## Desired change

- CSV: `staff-executive` → `actionsPerTurn 1`, `handSlotsAdded 1`, description updated to state the `+1` hand slot and `+1` action/week.
- Card art: regenerate `staff-executive.svg` and `csv-checksum.json`.

data.description:
# Intake Brief: Improved money/reputation animation

**Work item:** MS-0MUYT57J80021CWW · `feature` · `medium`

## Headline

When coins and reputation pips fly to the HUD they currently land on
hard-coded coordinates (`gameW * 0.25 + 70` for coins, `gameW * 0.5` for
reputation at `hudY`) instead of the actual on-screen position of the
"Coins: N" / "Reputation: N" numbers. The flights must end at the location of
the painted coin/reputation number.

## Problem statement

The HUD strip renders `Coins: N` left-aligned at `hudLeft + 10` and
`Reputation: N` left-aligned at `favourBandRight + 40` (positions derived from
the SLL layout and viewport, not fixed fractions of the screen width). Every
market of the codebase that animates coins/reputation to the HUD instead targets
static hard-coded fractions of `gameW`, so the landing point only coincidentally
coincides with the counters — and drifts (most noticeably for reputation, whose
number sits near the right of a label that can be wider than the assumed
position) whenever `hudLeft`/`favourBandRight` or the number of digits change.
The animation reads as coins "missing" the counter.

## Users

- **Player.** When a turn ends and coins/reputation resolve, the flying
  visuals should land on the counter numbers so the income visibly accrues
  into the player's totals.

### Example user story

> As a player, when I end a turn and coins/reputation fly to the HUD, I want
> them to land exactly on the Coins/Reputation numbers so I can see the income
> arrive in my totals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Accurate landing.** Every coin/reputation → HUD flight lands within a
   small tolerance (≤ 2px) of the on-screen centre of the corresponding
   numeric value — the coin number for coin flights, the reputation number for
   reputation pips — across the supported viewports and digit counts. This
   covers: end-of-turn income collection (`animateIncomeCollection` +
   `collectIncomeGrids`), the `upcoming` income phase (HUD coin/rep
   destinations), incident-reveal delta bubbles, and the sell refund coin fly.
2. **Single source of truth.** The HUD render publishes one live anchor for
   the coin number and one for the reputation number; all animators consume
   the published anchors. No `gameW * 0.25` / `gameW * 0.5` target literals
   remain in `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimator*`.
3. **Layout drift resilience.** Anchors are recomputed whenever the HUD is
   re-rendered (including viewport/window changes), so subsequent flights
   target the current number positions.
4. **Presentation-only.** The change never mutates game state, the turn
   transcript, or the deferred-mutation window; reduced-motion and
   replay/headless modes remain flight-free exactly as today. No change to
   flight pacing, staggered SFX, or the income-phase choreography.
5. **Tests + docs.** Unit tests assert flight destinations equal the published
   anchors (coin and reputation paths); a browser test asserts the published
   anchor matches the rendered number centre of `coinText`/`repText`. All
   related documentation is updated (including `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`
   and code comments). Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Presentation-layer only (defensive `try/catch` style preserved — a failing
  animator must never stall the turn).
- Must not change phased income pacing (~11s collection) or the
  `incomeCollectionActive` / deferred-delta timing windows.
- Must not regress the HUD layout geometry guards
  (`hud-strip-layout`, `hud-market-geometry-guard` browser suites).

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` lays out `Coins: N` at `hudLeft + 10`
  and `Reputation: N` at `favourBandRight + 40`, computing
  `repX = repText.x + repText.width / 2` (centre of the whole label, not the
  number) and passing `coinX: hudLeft + 70` to `animateHudValueChanges`.
- Animators hard-code HUD destinations as fractions of `gameW`:
  - `MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateIncomeCollection` (`coinX =
    gameW * 0.25 + 70`, `repX = gameW * 0.5`), `runIncomePhase` `upcoming`
    (`hudCoin`/`hudRep`), `collectIncomeGrids` (`coinX = gameW * 0.25 + 70`).
  - `MainStreetAnimatorBoard.ts` — sell refund (`coinX = gameW * 0.25 + 70`).
  - `MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — delta bubbles (`hudCoinX`/`hudRepX`).

## Desired change

- During HUD render, compute and publish the live coin-number and
  reputation-number anchor positions (numeric glyph centre, i.e. label
  origin + prefix width + number-width/2) — e.g. new fields on `SceneLayout`
  or transient scene fields set by `refreshHudStrip`.
- Replace the hard-coded flight destinations with the published anchors,
  falling back to the current approximate coordinate only when the anchor is
  not yet available (e.g. very first render).

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — compute + publish coin/reputation number anchors.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — extend `SceneLayout` (or add scene fields) for the anchors.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — consume anchors in `animateIncomeCollection`, `runIncomePhase` (`upcoming`), `collectIncomeGrids`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorBoard.ts` — consume coin anchor for the sell refund flight.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — consume anchors for incident delta bubbles.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — anchor storage/reset lifecycle.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-animator.test.ts`, `upcoming-flow-animation.test.ts`, `incident-reveal-animator.test.ts`, `sell-demolition-animator.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/hud-strip-layout.browser.test.ts` — destination assertions.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — document the anchor source of truth.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8** — "Coin and Reputation should count up/down"
  (in-progress, idea): end-of-turn reconciliation coins/rep fly to/from the
  HUD totals and the totals should count up/down as the animation plays.
  Complementary: that item animates the *numbers*; this item fixes where the
  flights *land*. Do not duplicate.
- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** — "Visual representation of reputation" (completed).
- **MS-0MUYGFWXK003QFYB** / **MS-0MUZ4WB290024ZGQ** — reputation income coin
  sources (pedestrian dissolve); origins only, destinations unchanged here.
- **CG-0MUA1UH3A008M4BS** — Upcoming/incident delta-flow routing (the
  `resolveDeltaFlow` destinations consumed by the upcoming + incident paths).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — scope:** "coins/reputation flying to the HUD" covers every
  flight path that ends at the HUD counters (income collection, Upcoming
  deltas, incident bubbles, sell refund). If the operator intended a narrower
  scope (e.g. income collection only), the ACs narrow accordingly.
- **Assumption — anchor:** "the location of the number" = the centre of the
  numeric portion of the HUD label, not the centre of the whole label.
- **Assumption — digit drift:** the anchor is captured at flight launch; a
  number that grows during a count-up animation is handled by the separate
  count-up/down work item (MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8), not here.
- **Risk:** anchor absent on the very first render (`previousCoins === null`
  path) — mitigate with a conservative fallback to the current approximate
  coordinate.
- **Risk — scope creep:** do not fold number count-up/down animation,
  new SFX, or pacing changes into this item; record any such opportunities as
  linked work items instead.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which flight paths are in scope?" — Answer (assumption, record by
  Map): all coin/reputation → HUD flights (income collection, Upcoming
  deltas, incident bubbles, sell refund). Source: work-item description
  wording "coins/reputation flying to the HUD"; repo inspection of all
  `gameW * 0.25 / 0.5` HUD destinations. OPEN QUESTION for the producer if a
  narrower scope is intended.
- Q: "What is 'the location of the coins/reputation number'?" — Answer
  (assumption, Map): the on-screen centre of the numeric value inside the
  `Coins: N` / `Reputation: N` label. Source: item wording; contrast with the
  current `repX` (whole-label centre) and `coinX` (`hudLeft + 70`).
- Q: "How should animators obtain the destination?" — Answer (assumption,
  Map): publish live anchors from the HUD render path; no duplicated
  hard-coded fractions. Source: outcome of duplicate-check + code inspection —
  the HUD already computes the real text positions.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUWE6MSQ006DEZ4** – End-reason & player-state model (completed)
- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** – Named storylines, outcome feedback & continuity indicator (completed)
- **MS-0MUO7CPH3003TXFI** – Reduce time upcoming event is shown (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 2px, absent, acceptance, actual, add (+246 more)
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: 0mtv9as15004ac1e, 0mua1uh3a008m4bs, 0muygfwxk003qfyb, 0muz4wb290024zgq, 11s (+224 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, actual, add, aligned (+208 more)
